title: `element_at` is 1-based and counts back from the end; `[]` is 0-based; out of range raises (ANSI)
verdict: `element_at(a, i)`: 1-based, negative from the end, 0 raises; out of range: raise (ANSI) or NULL
description: `element_at(a, i)` counts from 1 and a negative `i` from the end (`element_at([10, 20, 30], -1)` is 30). An index of 0 raises `INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO` in both modes. Past either end it raises `INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX_IN_ELEMENT_AT` under ANSI and is NULL without it; `try_element_at` gives NULL.
`a[i]` counts from 0 and has no negative indexes: `a[5]` and `a[-1]` raise `INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX` under ANSI and are NULL without it. `get(a, i)` is 0-based and NULL out of range in both modes.
`size(NULL)` and `cardinality(NULL)` are NULL under ANSI and -1 without it (`spark.sql.legacy.sizeOfNull` follows ANSI); `array_size(NULL)` is NULL in both.
reference: `list_extract(l, i)` (reference-semantics.md, Nested) counts from 1, as DuckDB's does. `element_at` matches it for positive indexes; a writer guards 0 and out-of-range indexes.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
